oneLiner: The dominant AI accelerator franchise, priced like a cyclical at its peak: at roughly 13-14x next-twelve-month EPS the market is not paying for growth, it is betting that FY2028 is the high-water mark. The stock works if earnings merely plateau after FY2028 rather than fall.
thesis: Full-stack lock-in. CUDA plus full-system integration (GPU + Vera CPU + NVLink + racks) and an annual Hopper-Blackwell-Rubin cadence keep rivals aiming at a moving target; Data Center was $89.0B (+117% YoY) in Q2 FY27.

Supply-limited growth. FY2028 was framed as ~70% growth with demand 'much higher', and supply commitments more than doubled q/q to $279B - management is buying capacity ahead of orders it believes it has.
Cheap against its own earnings path. The forward multiple sits far below the 30-40x band of 2023-2025, so the stock does not need a re-rating - only for earnings to hold up past FY2028.
China is a free option. H200 licences exist (~$10B approved) but Beijing has blocked purchases; guidance embeds roughly zero China Data Center revenue.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 FY2027 (ended Jul 26, 2026; reported Aug 26, 2026)
points: Revenue $96.2B, +106% YoY, +18% QoQ (~$5B above the $91B guide midpoint); Data Center $89.0B, +117% YoY.
GAAP gross margin 75.0%; operating margin 66.2% (operating income $63.7B, +124% YoY).

Guide: Q3 FY2027 revenue $108.0B plus or minus 2%, gross margin 74.0% plus or minus 50bp; zero China DC compute assumed. Call: FY2028 revenue guided to ~70% growth; supply commitments doubled q/q to $279B.

segments: Data Center ~93% of revenue ($89.0B in Q2 FY27, +117% YoY): Blackwell/GB300 is the volume platform; Vera Rubin now ramping into full production with racks running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud and Azure.
Edge Computing ~7% ($7.2B in Q2 FY27, +27% YoY): Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive; Microsoft partnership to put 1-petaflop RTX Spark into Windows PCs.

Strategic portfolio (new): $30B Intel stake and $21B SpaceX stake disclosed Aug 14, 2026 (June 30 marks; the Intel position was ~$22B by Aug 14 after Intel's $20B offering), plus a $1.5B investment in SB Energy.
competitive: AMD MI400 series narrows the hardware gap but trails on software ecosystem.
Custom ASICs are the most credible threat: Broadcom (Google TPU, Meta MTIA, OpenAI), Marvell (Trainium, Maia) take share-of-wallet at the largest, most concentrated buyers.
Cerebras (CBRS) IPO'd May 2026 with a 750MW OpenAI deal: small revenue but a validated wafer-scale inference alternative.
Hyperscaler in-house silicon (TPU v7, Trainium 3, Maia 2) grows faster than merchant GPUs in 2026 (TrendForce: +45% vs +16%).
Equity-and-financing ties (Intel co-development, SpaceX/xAI Colossus, OpenAI Ohio) lock large buyers to NVDA silicon in ways rivals cannot match - and invite circularity critiques.
moat: CUDA and the surrounding software stack, compounded by full-system integration competitors must replicate across six-plus co-designed chips, an annual platform cadence, and a 350+-factory supply chain ramped for Rubin. Increasingly reinforced by capital: equity stakes and financing guarantees that make NVDA the anchor allocator of the AI buildout.
risks: Customer concentration. Three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of Q1 FY27 revenue (54% combined); a single capex pause shows up in one quarter.
Cyclical peak. If FY2029 looks down, the market will value FY2028 EPS at a peak-cycle multiple (the bear case), whatever FY2028 itself delivers.

Earnings quality. Only ~70% of trailing net income has converted to operating cash, and net income now exceeds operating income because of investment gains; vendor financing ($105B Ohio backstop, stakes in chip buyers) blurs how much demand is self-funded.
Power and execution. Data center power, not chips, may cap 2027 deployments; a one-quarter Rubin slip moves FY2028 by tens of billions.

latestProse: Q2 FY2027 (ended Jul 26, 2026; reported Aug 26). Revenue $96.2B, ~$5B above the $91B guide midpoint, +106% YoY and +18% QoQ; Data Center $89.0B (+117%) is ~93% of the company. GAAP gross margin 75.0%, operating margin 66.2% (operating income $63.7B, +124% YoY). GAAP diluted EPS $2.46 (+128%); non-GAAP $2.22. The call's headline was supply, not demand: FY2028 revenue guided to ~70% growth ('we have supply for 70% growth; demand is much higher'), and supply commitments more than doubled q/q from $119B to $279B, mostly memory procurement. Vera Rubin is ramping into full production with racks running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud and Azure.
guidanceProse: Q3 FY2027 guide: revenue $108.0B plus or minus 2%, gross margin 74.0% plus or minus 50bp - another +12% sequential step, with zero China Data Center compute revenue assumed. On the call NVDA put a number on next year: FY2028 revenue growth of ~70%, framed as a supply figure with demand 'much higher'. The vendor-finance overlay stands: NVDA will backstop up to $105B for OpenAI's Ohio campus (8GW planned with SB Energy, first 800MW by 2028, ~1.5M NVDA GPUs and $150-200B of potential revenue per deployed generation through 2030, scaled back from ~$250B first discussed), alongside $500B+ of AI-infrastructure MOU capital with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR. China: H200 licensed (~$10B approved, 25% revenue share to the US government) but Beijing has blocked purchases - guidance embeds roughly zero China revenue, making it a free option.

verdict.summary: The debate is not whether NVDA grows next year (it guided ~70% FY2028 growth, supply-limited) but what happens after. A low-teens forward multiple already discounts a sharp earnings decline beyond FY2028, so the asymmetry favours owning it: the bear case needs both a capex digestion and margin compression to lose about a third, while delivering a bit less than the guide at a high-teens multiple returns ~20%. Two things would change this view: a hyperscaler capex pause in 2027 guidance, and earnings quality - only ~70% of trailing profit has turned into operating cash while vendor financing, equity marks and supply prepayments grow.
wtb: FY2028 revenue lands within ~10% of the ~70% growth framework (about $620-690B) - hyperscaler 2027 capex keeps rising rather than digesting.
Gross margin holds at or above ~72% through the Rubin ramp; each point is roughly $6B of FY2028 operating profit.
The market pays at least a mid-teens multiple on FY2028 EPS at end-2027, which only requires FY2029 to be flat to modestly down, not up.
Cash conversion recovers toward 85%+ as supply prepayments turn into shipped product, confirming the profit is cash and not financed demand.

bear.why: 2027 hyperscaler capex flattens after the 2026 surge; FY2028 revenue grows only ~18% on FY2027's ~$406B, custom ASICs take inference share at the top three customers and gross margin slips to ~70%. The market treats FY2028 as the peak and pays a peak-cycle multiple.

base.why: Rubin ramps on schedule but supply and power cap the year below the 70% framework (~+53%); net margin ~54% with gross margin ~73%. FY2029 visibility is mixed, so the multiple stays well below the 2023-25 range.

bull.why: The ~70% framework is met; 2027 capex guides rise again, agentic inference keeps clusters full and the Ohio/OpenAI pipeline converts to committed orders. FY2029 growth looks positive, earning a low-20s multiple.

scenarioModel.note: FY2027 revenue assumes Q1 $81.6B + Q2 $96.2B + Q3 guide $108B + ~$120B Q4 = ~$406B. EPS = revenue x net margin / ~24.1B diluted shares. Multiples are applied to FY2028 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is FY2028 the peak, or the middle of the cycle?
debates.bull: Supply, not demand, sets the ~70% FY2028 guide; supply commitments more than doubled q/q to $279B, and hyperscaler capex is tracking ~$725B in 2026 toward ~$1T in 2027 (Goldman Sachs tracking).
debates.bear: Capex at this scale has always digested; the 2027 increments are smaller in % terms, and three customers were 54% of Q1 FY27 revenue, so one pause shows up immediately.
debates.view: The price already assumes a peak - this debate decides the multiple (14x vs 22x), not whether the stock is cheap today. Watch 2027 capex language more than NVDA's own guide.

signpost.metric: Combined 2027 capex guidance from MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META
signpost.threshold: bullish if guided up 25%+ YoY; bearish if flat

debates.q: How much of the profit is cash?
debates.bull: The gap is timing: supplier prepayments for HBM and Rubin capacity buy share, and net income includes real gains on the Intel and SpaceX stakes.
debates.bear: Trailing operating cash flow is only ~70% of net income, net income now exceeds operating income, and NVDA is financing demand ($105B Ohio backstop, $50B+ of stakes in chip buyers). Reported EPS overstates the operating franchise.
debates.view: Legitimate but not yet a thesis-breaker: 70% conversion on $193B of profit is still $134B of cash. It becomes one if conversion falls further while receivables and prepayments keep rising.

signpost.metric: Q3 FY27 operating cash flow / net income; size of non-operating gains
signpost.threshold: below 65% for a second quarter = red flag

debates.q: Do custom ASICs cap NVDA's share at its biggest customers?
debates.bull: Full-system integration (GPU + Vera CPU + NVLink + racks) and CUDA are a moving target; merchant GPUs still take the largest share of every major cluster.
debates.bear: TrendForce sees hyperscaler in-house silicon growing ~45% vs ~16% for merchant GPUs in 2026; Broadcom and Marvell are winning exactly the three customers that matter.
debates.view: Margin share loss is in the base case; the bear case needs ASICs to take training, not just inference. Broadcom's AI guide is the cleanest read.

signpost.metric: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue growth vs NVDA Data Center growth
signpost.threshold: AVGO AI growth above 2x NVDA DC growth for two quarters
